starter/compliment: Any dye you like, dearie, on the house. Nearly.
Brought him back safe, you did. A witch remembers a kindness.
You're welcome at my cauldron any time, dearie. Mind the tomatoes.
starter/insult: Don't you go teaching my Jimmy any adventuring habits.
Saved my apprentice, and now you think you're owed. You are, a bit.
Still owe you, do I? Aggie's memory isn't what it was.
starter/remark: Jimmy, stir it the other way! Widdershins, boy!
The house is noisy again, and I'll not complain about it.
Two pairs of hands at the cauldron again. The dyes fairly fly out.

starter/compliment: There's my clever one. Got a prince out under a dab of paste!
You'd make a decent witch, my dear. You know what paste is for.
starter/insult: I'll bet you never picked a redberry for that paste yourself.
Saved a prince, did you? The fine for cheek is still the fine, dearie.
Who got the prince out? My paste. You just carried the pot.
starter/remark: Ash, flour, water, redberries. Good enough for a prince, apparently.
I make things pretty, mostly. Making a prince look ordinary was new.
Wonder if that prince ever washed my paste off. Shame if he did.

starter/compliment: Sensible sort, you. You'd not eat one of my tomatoes.
Such a pretty way about you, dearie. No paste needed.
You'd never call a witch names, would you, dearie? No, not you.
starter/insult: Don't make faces at Aggie. Faces have a way of sticking.
Rushing past a witch without so much as a hello? Brave, dearie.
That one'd make a fine newt. Not that I do that any more.
starter/remark: Paste wants stirring and muttering. The muttering's the important bit.
That professor's machine again, I'll bet. Heard a chicken talking.
Tried for a lesser demon once and got a tomato. They do bite, mind.

starter/compliment: A sensible one, at last. Sensible folk come home when they say.
If my Jimmy had half your sense, he'd be home by now.
That one looks like they could find anybody. Even a lost boy.
starter/insult: Don't wander off and not come back. I've one of those already.
Going off for supplies, are you? That's what Jimmy said.
Not seen my Jimmy, have you? No, you'd not notice a thing.
starter/remark: I'd go after him myself, but I can't leave till he's back.
If anyone's hurt that boy, they'll wake up a very odd shape.
Jimmy the Chisel, odd name for a witch's apprentice. Good boy, though.

starter/compliment: Ah, my best customer! A beard, a headdress, and never a complaint.
My friend! You went all the way to Pollnivneach. A true tourist.
Such a good sport, my friend! Not everyone enjoys a little tourism.
starter/insult: A false beard went to your head, my friend. It happens to tourists.
Still no assistant, and you walk past a perfectly good job, my friend.
You crossed the desert for my nephew? And you paid for the beard!
starter/remark: Farid at the Exchange, Baba in hiding. My family does get about.
Hiding, the boy is. The best salesmen always have to hide a while.
The mayor and I understand each other. Men of business, both of us.

starter/compliment: For you, my friend, a special price. I say that to almost nobody.
With an eye like yours you could sell. Nearly as well as me, even.
starter/insult: An adventurer with nothing to buy? Every adventurer needs a tinderbox.
Haggling by walking away, my friend? I invented that trick.
I could sell you a bucket you do not need. I could sell you two.
starter/remark: I never buy, my friend. Buying is how a merchant becomes poor.
Sell a carpet? And have every rug merchant fly for himself? Never.
The gnomes say my carpets will never take off. My carpets disagree.

starter/compliment: For a friend like you, the robes are nearly half price. Nearly.
Now there goes someone who would get to Pollnivneach and back.
You would make a fine assistant. Better than the one who never came.
starter/insult: I would hire you myself, my friend, but I would have to watch you.
My nephew is lost somewhere, and you are lost in front of my stall.
Not interested? I shall put you down as 'later', my friend.
starter/remark: Family is family, my friend, but punctual family is better.
There is a nephew-shaped gap behind my counter, my friend.
Who minds the stall while I sell? Not my nephew, apparently.

starter/compliment: Only you would go. I shall remember that, my friend, at a discount.
With my headdress on, they will take you for a local. Nearly.
You bargain badly but you travel well. I respect the second.
starter/insult: Did the beard fall off already? I do not do refunds.
Lost the way? Buy some papyrus from me and draw yourself a map.
The boy will have grown a real beard by the time you get there.
starter/remark: I keep a spare false beard for emergencies. One never knows.
My nephew will be so pleased to meet a stranger in a false beard.
When the boy arrives I shall take a day off... no, I shall sell more.

starter/compliment: Did for that old guardian, they tell me. Proper job, that.
Go on, use the finished half of the bridge. You've earned it.
That's the one who sorted the Nexus. Shift the plank, let them by.
You helped take the Nexus, pal? Then you can walk my bridge first.
starter/insult: Don't stand there looking heroic. Looking heroic won't hold up a wall.
Saved the whole archive and still too grand to hand me a nail, pal.
Took the Nexus, did you? The Nexus didn't need a roof. My camp does.
Treasure for the heroes and splinters for us. Fair's fair, I suppose.
starter/remark: Crystal rocks sinking and popping up again. Can't lay a floor on that.
Goblins with a siege engine. I'd give a week's pay to see the joints.
Somebody's got to build the walls the soldiers stand behind, pal.
Somebody's walked off with my mallet. A soldier, I'll bet.
Whoever started this place gave up halfway. Not me. Not my bridge.

starter/compliment: Not stood gawping at my bridge. I like that in a person.
Steady on their feet, that one. Wouldn't fall off a half-done bridge.
That one's actually going in. Rather them than me, I'll say that.
You look like you'd carry a beam without being asked twice.
starter/insult: Admiring the ravine? It's a hole, pal. Holes don't need admiring.
All that fighting and you'd not know which end of a nail goes in.
Don't lean on that rail. It's not a rail yet, it's a hope.
If you're going to stand there, hold the end of this. No? Thought not.
That one walked through my fresh mortar, I'd swear to it.
starter/remark: Guthix's followers left this place half built. I know how that goes.
Plank, plank, rope... where's the rope gone? Somebody's had my rope.
Plenty of swords in this camp. Not a hammer among them, mind.
Word from the knights is we're barely holding. So, faster hammers.

starter/compliment: Ah, friend. All that fuss, and nobody actually died.
Not your fault the lad's a fool. The plan was sound.
You'd make a fair apothecary's runner. Pity I can't afford one.
starter/insult: Back for another dead-looking potion? One per customer, I think.
Mind that one. Last time, somebody ended up in a crypt.
Some matchmaker. The lad left with the cousin.
starter/remark: My potion worked a treat. Too well, by Romeo's account.
No call for cadava potions now. Strength potions again, then.
Nobody asks what goes in a cadava potion twice.

starter/compliment: If I gave out free potions, you'd be first in line. I don't, mind.
That one would never call me out for nothing. Unlike Unferth.
starter/insult: After something for nothing? The only cure for that is work.
Ingredients, not excuses. I've had enough excuses this week.
Someone like you would eat a cadava berry to see what happens.
starter/remark: Another crate of doctor's hats, and still nobody calls me doctor.
Cadava berries look good enough to eat. That's rather the trouble.
Unferth's ill again, apparently. I'll go. I always go.

starter/compliment: You could talk sense into someone, I'd say. Romeo, for instance.
You look the sensible sort. Not lovesick, at least.
starter/insult: Need a potion? Bring ingredients. Wanting one isn't an ingredient.
Strength potion? You'll want two. Or a different line of work.
You're not lovesick as well, are you? One Romeo's plenty.
starter/remark: All quiet. Apart from Romeo's woman trouble, which is loud.
No potion for Romeo's trouble. I've looked.
Quiet week. Nobody ill, nobody poisoned. Dreadful for trade.

starter/compliment: Good of you to help, and for the girl's sake, I hope, not Romeo's.
Not many would run about for a lovesick lad. Decent of you.
You'll keep a secret, I think. Good. This potion needs one.
starter/insult: Mind the berries. You've the look of someone who snacks.
Running errands for Romeo now? You'll be writing his letters next.
You do know you're not meant to drink it? Just checking.
starter/remark: A potion to look dead is easy to brew. Explaining it is the hard part.
Horn of dog is harder to come by than you'd think. Don't ask.
Pink berries from the mining pit. Don't eat them on the way, mind.

starter/compliment: History forgot Wally. I'll see to it that it doesn't forget you.
There's my hero. The ball shows a quieter city, thanks to you.
Wally's sword found a worthy hand again. He'd have liked you, dear.
starter/insult: Beat a demon, and still you can't guess what I'll say next.
I'd tell you your future, young one, but you'd only go and spoil it.
starter/remark: A good bit of demon-slaying, that. Wally would have approved.
Guthix was with the young one after all. I did ask him nicely.
Wally still gets no song, mind. Some things the ball can't mend.

starter/compliment: An old soul in one so young... well, younger than me, but who isn't?
Wisdom in the young! Ye gods, I'd almost given up looking.
You'll go far, young one. I'd say how far, but you'd only check.
starter/insult: I asked the ball about you, dear. It went cloudy and stayed that way.
Too late for a fortune, young one. You've already done the daft thing.
Your future costs silver. Your past is free, and it's muddy.
starter/remark: Another coin, another future. Nobody likes the ones about rain.
Count the stool legs in the Blue Moon... no, I've said too much.
Not their night in the Wilderness, I tell them. Off they go anyway.

starter/compliment: I've been waiting for a face like yours. Well, waiting for a face.
The city will need a brave young one soon. You'd do nicely, I think.
You've the look of someone who could hold a silver sword, young one.
starter/insult: I foresaw a hero. I did not foresee the hero dawdling in the square.
The ball says you'll be brave one day. It didn't say which day.
Wally was young once too. Mind, he had a sword and some sense.
starter/remark: Evil sorcerers. Always the stone circle, never anywhere pleasant.
Sir Prysin has the sword now. I do hope he's been dusting it.
Somebody's chanting at the stone circle. I can feel it in my teeth.

starter/compliment: I knew you'd take it on, dear. I didn't need the ball for that one.
Keys and wizards and all that bother, and still you're going. Good.
That one will do. I said so to the ball, and the ball agreed.
starter/insult: Delrith's waited ages. Seems he'll wait a bit longer for this one.
Lost a key already, dear? The ball rather suggested you might.
The ball shows you at the circle, and then running the other way.
starter/remark: Delrith stirs. I feel it in the ball, and in my knees.
Not now, dear, I'm watching the circle.
Wally did it once, so somebody can do it again. Somebody had better.

starter/compliment: Ah, my favourite courier! Mind you, I'd still sell you a rune.
For you, adventurer, the good tea. The rest get the dusty sort.
Sedridor speaks well of you, I'd wager. He certainly ought to.
starter/insult: Back for another free trip? I'll start charging tea money.
The incantation isn't long, but you'd still muddle it, I expect.
starter/remark: Must lock away the coded notes. Both sets. Now especially.
Tea, then the mine, then more tea. That's the order of things now.
The old tower lost those words when it burned. Now I say them daily.

starter/compliment: An honest face. I'd trust you with my death runes. Nearly.
Careful sort, are you? Good. Runecraft rewards the careful.
I'll sell you the cape one day, I shouldn't wonder.
starter/insult: Do you know what a rune is? No, no, it's fine. Most don't.
I'd offer you tea, but you look like you'd spill it on the stock.
Mind runes for you, I'd guess. For, ah... the mind.
starter/remark: Body runes. Little treasures. Hardly anyone buys them.
Kettle's on, if anyone wants tea. Anyone at all.
Reldo still has my book on... no, I have his. One of us has it.

starter/compliment: A clever-looking sort. The chaos runes are just there, if you like.
An adventurer who stops at a rune shop! There's hope for you yet.
You look like a reader. Reldo would like you, and so do I.
starter/insult: Fire runes and elbows don't mix. Somebody always learns that here.
Runes don't grow on trees, you know. I'm asked weekly.
You look like you'd use a death rune to light a fire. Please don't.
starter/remark: Quiet day. Even the air runes look bored.
Runecraft started a whole new age. Not bad for a little stone.
Tea for one again. Customers do rush off.

starter/compliment: Ah, back again! Any news? No, no, don't let me keep you.
Tea, adventurer? You've earned it, running about for us rune folk.
You've a head for secrets. I'd trust you with my coded notes.
starter/insult: Any slower, and the old tower would have rebuilt itself.
Can you read code? No? Good, that's rather the point.
Conclusions are for later. You, I see, have jumped to several.
starter/remark: If Sedridor's discovery fits my notes... no, no. Too soon to say.
Tea's gone cold again. Research does that.
The shop can mind itself today. I've research on.

starter/compliment: Good to see you. It's a long day standing about, and you brighten it.
If they ever write a poem about this place, I hope you're in it.
Oh, hello. You're the one who made this place safe enough to read in.
There goes the one who held the archive, and so quietly. I like that.
Your things, ready as ever. The least I can do after the vault.
starter/insult: Another trip down the chasm? You must like danger more than I do.
Back again? I'd only just found my page.
Held the Nexus, and still you can't keep a tidy bank.
I'd recommend a book, but I've seen how you treat your bank.
Such a hurry, always. The cavern will still be here, you know.
starter/remark: Now we're settled, the hardest part of my day is choosing a poem.
Quiet today. Only the odd demon, by all accounts.
The alliance always picks somewhere dangerous. I've stopped asking.
Thought to be from the Second Age, this book. It's held up well.
Wherever the alliance goes next, I do hope it has a garden.

starter/compliment: It's nice to see someone come down here on purpose. Brave of you.
Oh, hello! Back in one piece, which is how I like my customers.
Oh, it's you. That's the nicest thing to walk past all morning.
You go where it's dangerous so the rest of us can stand about. Thanks.
You'd like this poem, I think. No, I won't read it out, but you would.
starter/insult: Back so soon? The cavern and I were just getting comfortable.
I came all this way so you'd have your things. Do try to use them.
Take your time in your bank. I've a long poem on the go.
You do know the defence is barely holding? Of course you do, carry on.
starter/remark: Everyone's things are here, safe. It's the people I worry about.
I like seeing the world. I'd just like to see more of the top of it.
I've admired this cavern from every angle now. All of them stone.
Still unpacking the bank boxes. Then comes the standing about.
The roots round those crystals are the closest thing to a garden here.

starter/compliment: Human could be general, maybe. Small general. Under me.
Human want beetle pie? Me share. Me not share with Wartface.
Look, Wartface! Armour fixer back. That one got brain.
starter/remark: Me miss shouting red. Brown not good word for shouting.
Me so bored, me nearly agree with Wartface. Nearly.
Wartface see brown on Grubfoot, then say brown his idea. Ha!

starter/compliment: Human walk past Wartface and not laugh. Good manners, that.
Me give human victory salute. Not silly bow like Wartface do.
Not one stupid question from human yet. Best human all day.
starter/insult: Human follow me about like Grubfoot. Me not need two Grubfoots.
Me seen cleverer rocks, human. Rocks not wander into hut.
Wartface! Look at this one. Nearly ugly as Wartface!
starter/remark: Goblins always win. Even when goblins lose, goblins win.
Wartface fat. Me not tell him quiet. Me tell him loud.
Where me put puzzle box? Wartface sit on it, probably.

starter/compliment: Human got opinion, me can tell. Better than Grubfoot.
Wartface, see this one? Clever. Wartface hate clever.
starter/insult: Grubfoot! Who let this one in? Shut up, Grubfoot. Me know.
starter/remark: Green? Green make goblin look like no armour at all!
Red. Red. Red. Me say it till Wartface go deaf.
Wartface say goblins listen to him. Half village in red! Ha!

starter/compliment: Good human. Me tell Mudknuckles give you worm stew. Me not want it.
Human cleverer than both generals. No. Than Wartface.
starter/insult: Human look lost. Dye that way, maybe. Or that way.
starter/remark: Green armour? Me rather wear nothing. Look same anyway.
Me tell human go north for dye. Human come back! Good, maybe.
Where dye come from? Me not know. Me general, not dye goblin.

starter/compliment: My hall is your hall now. Do not drink it dry.
The name I gave you suits you. I am rarely wrong about names.
You earned what most of my people were simply handed at birth.
starter/remark: Call us barbarians now, and one more of us will answer back.
Koschei passed his trials too. I still fear he will remember and go.
Seven elders voted! It is not every winter I name a new one.

starter/insult: Do not even think of a joke about my helm. I can see it coming.
I expect you cast a spell to tie your boots, like the Moon Clan.
starter/remark: A dent in this helm for every fight. It is mostly dents now.
All men were Fremennik once, before some got greedy for rune rocks.
Pah! The Moon Clan cannot boil water without a spell.

starter/compliment: If any outerlander could win seven elders, it might be you.
Outerlander is no insult, you understand. Least of all for you.
starter/insult: An outerlander in my hall. Keep your hands off the kegs.
Outerlanders call us barbarians, and then ask us the way.
Seven elders would have to vote for you. Start with the friendliest.
starter/remark: As chieftain I say who speaks with outerlanders. Mostly I say no.
Outerlanders gawp at our hall as if they had never seen a roof.
Twelve elders on the council, and not one agrees on breakfast.

starter/compliment: Mark that one. Stubborn as a Fremennik already.
Still outerlander, aye, but I say it fondly now.
There is more Fremennik in you than in some born here.
starter/insult: Do not come crying to me about the elders. I only rule here.
Half a Fremennik, you are. The worse half, so far.
Seven votes? You could not win a drinking contest, outerlander.
starter/remark: A chieftain does not tip the council's scales. Not even a little.
If the vote goes well, the hall will drink. If not, the hall drinks.
The council will vote when it votes. I am only chieftain.

starter/compliment: Good honest ore you brought me. Not a speck of rubbish in it.
Nurmof's order went out on time, friend, and that's thanks to you.
The pickaxes from your copper are some of my best, friend.
starter/insult: That one's welcome at my anvils and my door. Just not in my wheat.
There's always work fetching clay, friend, if adventuring dries up.
Use my anvils by all means, friend. Do try not to dent them.
starter/remark: A few coins for all that ore. Ought to have been more, really.
Both anvils ringing again. That's the sound of a happy smithy.
Someone's been at my anvils again. Good. That's what they're for.

starter/compliment: Good manners, traveller. That's a rarer metal than mithril.
Polite and unhurried. You'd get on with the lads in the mine.
There goes someone who knows good iron from bad, I'd wager.
starter/insult: Do mind the anvils, traveller. They've more manners than some.
I'd offer you the whetstone, traveller, but it wants a steady hand.
You'll want a bit more mining practice before you try iron, I'd say.
starter/remark: Another crop circle in the wheat. I do wish they'd ask first.
Quiet out here, just me and the wheat. Suits me fine.
That's another pickaxe head done. Nice even temper on this one.

starter/compliment: There's someone who could carry six lumps of clay and not grumble.
starter/insult: Iron ore's in the mine, traveller, should you ever feel useful.
Off for a stroll? Bring back some clay if you trip on any.
starter/remark: All that clay just inside the mine, and here I sit without a lump.
Nurmof will be wanting his order, and me short of copper.
Pickaxe heads don't cast themselves, more's the pity.

starter/compliment: A helper with manners! I'd almost forgotten there were such folk.
Iron's no small thing, and you're having a go anyway. Good for you.
That's the spirit! The lads below will take you for one of theirs.
starter/insult: If you'd sooner buy the iron, traveller, I'll not tell a soul.
No hurry, traveller. My anvils are used to waiting.
You're very welcome to dawdle, traveller. Nurmof's the one waiting.
starter/remark: Heard a pickaxe ringing in the mine. That'll be my helper, I expect.
I've cleared a space for the ore. Hopeful of me, perhaps.
Kept the casts out. Won't need them till the clay comes.

starter/compliment: I bless every traveller who passes. You, I bless twice.
There goes one I would gladly see in the robes of a priest.
You walked into Mort Myre and came out still yourself. Bless you.
starter/insult: I said there was something of the faith in you. A small something.
Out in that swamp so long, I feared you'd come back a Guthixian.
starter/remark: Guthixians would call that swamp balance. I call it rot.
I pray the ghasts go hungry tonight. Travellers too often do.
The Seven fought ten days without sleep. I nod off at my prayers.

starter/compliment: I think the Seven would have found room for one like you.
Not many come this near the Salve on purpose. Good for you.
Saradomin keep you, adventurer. The road east is not a kind one.
starter/insult: Crossing into Morytania without a prayer? How very brave.
You have the air of one who skips prayers. I shall pray for two.
You'd not be a Guthixian, would you? You have that look.
starter/remark: A priest's work is mostly prayer and sweeping. Mostly sweeping.
Hard to believe that swamp was ever a lovely forest. Yet it was.
The ghasts take your food first, and then they take you.

starter/compliment: I have prayed for you every night since. It seems to be working.
Keep my family's dagger close, friend. You earned it.
Veliaf would like you, I think. He likes very few.
starter/insult: Every time you visit, something needs blessing afterwards.
Saved the temple, and still you walk past the altar. Tsk.
Someone fetch a broom. The saviour of Paterdomus is back.
starter/remark: I set a place for Filliman some evenings. He never comes now.
Is Filliman eating, out there? Druids do forget.
That well will not be fouled again while I draw breath.

starter/compliment: Mind the stairs, my rescuer. I need you in one piece.
Saradomin chose well when he sent you up those stairs.
You came! Saradomin heard me after all, adventurer.
starter/insult: Forgive me, but are you quite sure which side you are on?
Oh, take your time. I have only a vampyre for company.
Still here, adventurer. Still locked in. In case you wondered.
starter/remark: Such a fine view from up here. I would trade it for a door.
The Seven held for ten days and nights. I can hold a little longer.
The lid moved in the night, I am sure of it. Or I dreamt it.

starter/compliment: Thank you. Guthix's things are safe again, for a while at least.
That one faced Ocellus in the vault, and walked out again.
You fought to defend it, not to own it. That's our way, near enough.
You stood against Ocellus for the balance. We won't forget it.
You'd make a fair druid, I think. You know when to stop.
starter/insult: Hero of the vault, and still you step on every root.
Nature thanks you. It would thank you more if you'd wipe your boots.
Ocellus thought only Guthix worthy of that blade. Don't get ideas.
Saved the archive, then straight to the chests. Balance, I suppose.
That one's pack is heavier coming out than going in, I'd wager.
starter/remark: A broken blade on a vine, still thick with power. Strange fruit.
Ivy would take the Dagon'hai as allies now. Balance is a hard road.
Ocellus was set to guard the Blade, not want it. Even guardians fall.
Those artefacts are like fire, Ivy says. Slowly, or not at all.

starter/compliment: All the way down the Chasm of Tears to help us, that one. Good heart.
Here to defend it, not to take it. That's the right way round.
Ivy Sophista sent for you. That's no small thing, among us.
You walk softly for an adventurer. The roots don't seem to mind you.
You've a balanced look about you. Not too much of anything.
starter/insult: Break nothing in the archive, please. It's older than your manners.
Do mind the roots. They're holding more together than you are.
Here to help, are you? Not to fill a sack like the rest? We'll see.
You've the look of someone who'd mine those crystals bare.
starter/remark: Looters from every side, each one sure the archive should be theirs.
The roots hold those crystals so tightly. Something wants them kept.

starter/compliment: Brave and not reckless, after all. I did wonder, about the dragon.
By Saradomin, the dragon my father feared is gone. I've you to thank.
To think Crandor's dragon fell to someone who walks past my door.
starter/insult: Father posted lookouts for a dragon. I may yet post one for you.
starter/remark: Crandor without its dragon. I wonder if word will come from it again.
Elvarg slain, with one of my shields. I like to think it helped.
Shields for the worthy, I always said, and for once I was right.

starter/compliment: A mine found through my talisman and your feet. A fine partnership.
Ah, the one who took my talisman across! A whole mine, they tell me.
I chose well with you. One so rarely gets to say that.
starter/insult: Back again? I've no more talismans, I'm afraid, only spoons.
Credit where it's due, adventurer. Rather more of it is mine.
One delivery, and you think yourself a wizard. Hmm?
starter/remark: I wonder if the wizards would name a seam after me. Probably not.
Rune essence, the wizards call it. Terribly important, I'm told.
The wizards have their mine, and I've an empty shelf where it sat.

starter/compliment: My father would have had someone like you up on the roof, watching.
Should a truly worthy cause arise... I'd think of you for a shield.
The peasantry could learn a great deal from your bearing.
starter/insult: Another adventurer. You'll be wanting a shield too, I suppose.
I would send you on an errand, but I'm rather fond of the errand.
You'll forgive me if I don't stand. One stands for the worthy.
starter/remark: Cook says the new range burns less. I've yet to taste the evidence.
Errands, errands, and never once can I run one myself.
Father kept lookouts on the roof for Elvarg. I miss the company.

starter/compliment: Free to come and go, aren't you? One could do great things with that.
Good heavens, a capable face. The castle has been short of those.
I'd trust you as far as the Wizards' Tower, and that's a fair way.
starter/insult: Adventurers come and go, and not one of them asks about talismans.
I'd ask your help, but I fear you'd sell the thing in Varrock.
You'd lose a talisman before the bridge, I expect.
starter/remark: Ancient, this talisman, or else very dirty.
The Wizards' Tower is hardly far. For someone else, that is.
What does one do with a talisman? I've polished it, for a start.

starter/compliment: Hey! Thanks again for getting my sample to Guidor in one piece.
I worry less with you about. Only a little less, mind.
You went to the king for me. Not many would knock on that door.
starter/insult: All that way with my sample and you didn't drop it. Miracles happen.
All the way to the king, and back with nothing to tell me?
You won't tell me what the king said. Fine. I'll guess, loudly.
starter/remark: Quiet day. A burn and a splinter. I could get used to quiet.
The king had that wall built. He knows why, even if I don't.
Who invents a plague? Honestly, the trouble it must take.

starter/compliment: Mind yourself out there. I'd rather not be patching you up.
You help people for nothing, don't you? I can always tell.
starter/insult: If you must fall off something, do it near a healer.
Some people test things first. Others become adventurers.
starter/remark: Guidor still sends to Rimmington for his chemicals. Creature of habit.
Nobody ever thanks whoever boils the bandages.
Now, did I label that sample? I'm sure I labelled it.

starter/compliment: Not many would brave the west side. You have, apparently.
Someone who isn't a mourner! That makes a nice change.
starter/insult: Are you lost, or just sightseeing the plague houses?
Don't mind me. I'll just be down here, being kidnapped.
You're very brave to wander about here. Or you haven't heard.
starter/remark: A cellar. Of all the places to be locked up, a damp cellar.
I only came over the wall to nurse people. Look where it got me.
Riddled with plague, this house? Not so much as a sneeze.

starter/compliment: Get me out and I'll stitch anything you like, free.
Hey, you found the place! That can't have been easy.
Someone's actually coming for me. Fancy that.
starter/insult: A rescue! At last. I'd started naming the cobwebs.
Any chance of a key today, or shall I get comfortable?
Oh good, a rescuer. Are they all this leisurely?
starter/remark: Footsteps upstairs again. Please let it be someone with a key.
I keep counting the bricks. There are a great many bricks.
Who kidnaps a nurse? What did they think I'd do, bandage them?

starter/compliment: A warlock's mischief, undone by a passer-by. Saradomin does provide.
I mention you in my prayers, traveller. Most evenings, anyway.
You were braver in that graveyard than I ever was, my friend.
starter/insult: Good work with the ghost. Now, about your own soul...
starter/remark: Must write to Urhney and tell him. He'll pretend not to care.

starter/compliment: Bless you for passing my door without a sneer. Not everyone does.
You'd make a fine letter-carrier for the Wise Old Man, I think.
You've heard of Saradomin, I can tell. What a relief!
starter/insult: A short sermon would do you good, traveller, a very short one.
Rushing past a house of Saradomin? He does notice, you know.
You look like you'd get stuck up a bell rope. Takes one to know one.
starter/remark: Is it 'smile upon' or 'shine upon'? Smile, I think.
Saradomin made the world with his brothers. He's the tidy one.
Two hundred and thirty years, this church. The roof feels them all.

starter/compliment: A good soul like yours would put any ghost at its ease, I think.
Saradomin's light is in you. Ghosts can't abide that, I hope.
You don't look like a ghost would frighten you. It frightens me.
starter/insult: Adventurers fight dragons all day, but a little ghost? Suddenly busy.
Don't let the ghost see you dawdling. It'll think you're staying.
Ghost-shy, are we? There's no shame in it, or only a little.
starter/remark: Avaunt, I said to it. It didn't avaunt.
Not a wicked ghost, I think. Just a very persistent one.
Something cold went past me in the graveyard. I didn't look round.

starter/compliment: Ah, there you are again, in and out of my graveyard like a regular.
Bless you for taking on our ghost. Saradomin smile on the work.
That's the one seeing to our ghost. Saradomin keep them.
starter/insult: I prayed for help, and Saradomin sent you. He does test us.
Some of us would like to bury people in peace, traveller.
Taking your time with that ghost, aren't you? It isn't going anywhere.
starter/remark: I've lit a candle for the ghost, and one for whoever's helping.
I've stopped saying good night to the graveyard. It answers.
Things are moving, Saradomin be praised. Slowly, but moving.

starter/compliment: Decent folk, you, even if you do hear voices about birds.
Keen eyes, you've got. See things that aren't there, but keen.
You meant well, with your penguins. I'll give you that much.
starter/insult: Don't you go poking my sheep for feathers, you scoundrel.
If you're wanting birds, try Seth Groats. He's got loads.
There goes the one who thinks my ewes have beaks.
starter/remark: If one of my sheep starts squawking, then I'll worry. Not before.
Sheep don't waddle. I've farmed long enough to know that much.
The Thing's bad enough without folk adding penguins to it.

starter/compliment: My sheep don't run from you now. That's trust, that is.
Sheared 'em neat, you did. Not a bald patch in the flock.
That one sheared my whole flock without a word of moaning.
starter/insult: If you've come for more coin, the gate's behind you. Shut it.
Paid what I promised, near enough. Stop looking at me like that.
Took your time with that wool. The sheep grew it back faster.
starter/remark: Can see their legs again. Never knew sheep had such knobbly knees.
Paid up, I did. Hurt, but I did it.
The Thing didn't like the shearing, or the sheep didn't. Same thing.

starter/compliment: Not after my livestock, are you? No, you've an honest look.
You don't look like a scoundrel. Not much, anyway.
You'd not fear The Thing, I reckon. Not that it's real... it is.
starter/insult: Adventurers. All swords and no shears.
Get off my land. No, that's the road... get off my road, then.
Lost, are you? On a road with a castle at the end of it?
starter/remark: Counted the flock twice, got two answers. That's The Thing, that is.
Gate's open again. I know I shut that gate.
Honest work never hurt anyone. Watching it hurts even less.

starter/compliment: A body could do worse than you, round a farm.
Them sheep took to you! They don't take to anybody.
You look like you'd know one end of a sheep from the other.
starter/insult: Don't you go near my sheep with a sword. It's shears they want.
There goes another one too grand for wool.
Your sort would sooner kill a sheep than shear one.
starter/remark: Any woollier and they'll float off in a stiff wind.
I'd shear 'em myself, only... no, I wouldn't.
Some payment, I said. I never said how much.

starter/compliment: Now there's someone I'd give any chamber to without a second look.
The troops talk about you, you know. Mostly kindly.
You faced Ocellus in the vault and walked out. That goes on the board.
starter/insult: Armacus is a good judge of character. He has his off days, of course.
Every hero in the lobby wants a word. Few want a chamber.
If you're waiting for a parade, the builders haven't built one.
Some adventurers rest on their laurels. You've brought a cushion.
starter/remark: A whole squad, and a single knight. I still don't like that report.
Armacus says evil is on the back foot. I'd like that in writing.
Fresh troops in, wounded out. The rota never stops down here.
Ivy doubts Ocellus is truly dead. I've left room on the board for him.

starter/compliment: If the Nexus can be taken, I'd wager you're the one to take it.
Newcomers usually need the plan twice. You had it the first time.
The line is thin, but it's a deal thicker with you on it.
starter/insult: Ah, our adventurer. The plan rather depends on you leaving the lobby.
Do stop admiring the board. It works better if somebody acts on it.
I've briefed raw recruits who left the lobby quicker than you.
They've a huge ork and a siege engine. We have you, which is a start.
starter/remark: Goblins with a siege engine. I never thought I'd put that on a board.
One scout came back from that lone knight. One, out of a whole squad.
Six chambers, all open to the Nexus. I'd sooner have two.
Skeletons and Zamorakian mages at war in the deep tunnels. Let them.

starter/compliment: Into the Lumber Yard for my cat! Not many would, dear.
That's the one who found my Fluffs, that is. Saved my wits.
You do your bit, dear. I like that in a person. And in a cat.
starter/insult: After another reward, dear? I've only kittens, and plenty of those.
Medals are for cats who catch rats, dear. None for people, I'm afraid.
starter/remark: Fluffs looks at me as if I'm the one who went missing. Cats!
Kittens to spare, if anyone wants one. Fed and stroked, mind.
Medal's ready for the next young cat that does its bit with the rats.

starter/compliment: A good sort, you. The sort who'd stop for a stray. Not a dog, mind.
Bob would take to that one, I'll bet. He's a fine judge, that cat.
Well well! A helpful-looking sort. Not like my boys, bless them.
starter/insult: I'd not trust you with a kitten. A goldfish, perhaps. Just about.
My boys have better manners, and my boys have none.
You look like you'd forget to feed a cat, then blame the cat.
starter/remark: Another stray kitten on the step. Well, I can't leave it there, can I?
Bob was a kitten in a basket once. Look at him now, the great lump.
Shilop! Wilough! Out of that sewer this instant! Oh, crumbs.

starter/compliment: Crumbs, you look capable. I've lost something, you know. Furry.
Sharp eyes, dear. Keep them open for a lost cat, would you?
You look like a cat-finder, dear. Do you find cats? I think you do.
starter/insult: Don't you go in that sewer looking for her. You'd only need fetching.
Off adventuring while poor Fluffs is out there. Well, don't mind me.
You've not seen a cat, have you? No. You'd have tripped over it.
starter/remark: If those boys know where Fluffs is, they'll want paying. By me!
Nearly ten years she's purred at my side, and now not a whisker.
Oh dear, oh dear. Who's going to sit on my knitting now?

starter/compliment: Bless you for trying, dear. Most people only say they'll look.
My boys could learn a thing or two from you. Mostly manners.
Paid my boys, did you? Oh, you're too good. They're terrors.
starter/insult: Did my boys fleece you? They did, didn't they? Oh, dear.
Fluffs hides from people who stomp. Some people stomp.
Shilop could've found her quicker, and he can't find his own boots.
starter/remark: Any news of Fluffs? No? No. I'll put the kettle on.
I hope those two didn't charge much. They will have. Little monkeys.
Shilop says he knows nothing. Shilop always knows something.

starter/compliment: Ah, our island explorer! The new room downstairs is half your doing.
If the fossils could talk, they'd thank you. I'll have to do instead.
You've the museum's spirit, you know. Off to an island for old bones!
starter/insult: Don't climb the skeletons. The children do quite enough of that.
Mind the fossils, please. They've lasted ages without your elbows.
Our island explorer, back to read the labels like everyone else.
starter/remark: A palaeontology room downstairs! My word, I still get lost in it.
Children adore the new bones. I do wish they'd stop climbing them.
Must finish the labels downstairs. One can't have unlabelled bones.

starter/compliment: History will remember you, I'm sure. I'll write the card myself.
I wrote your half-certificate in my best hand, you know.
There's a slice of cake with your name on it, shield-finder.
starter/insult: One shield, and now you think you're an archaeologist. Pish-posh.
The reward's been paid, if that's why you're lingering.
You found half the shield. Shall I put half your name on the card?
starter/remark: Back in its case, and hardly a scratch. Well, a crack down the middle.
Half-certificates! I'd never written one before. Rather proud of them.
Two halves of a shield, and two finders to match. How tidy.

starter/compliment: A student of the past, are we? There's cake for those who pass.
You look like you've dug something up in your time. Do tell!
starter/insult: Adventurers, looking for treasure in a museum. It's all labelled!
Passed your exams yet? No? The cake will keep. Probably.
The macabre relics are over there, if that's more your sort of thing.
starter/remark: Macabre inscriptions on these shipwreck relics. Lovely, though.
Seven priestly warriors, and I still say the display undersells them.
The museum goes to great lengths for a treasure. Great lengths!

starter/compliment: My word, an honest face! The Phoenix Gang never had one of those.
Now that one has a sense of history. Rarer than a shield, nowadays.
You'd look rather good on a plaque. Returned by... well, we'll see.
starter/insult: Not a Phoenix, I hope? You've a slightly shifty look about you.
The king's reward is for the shield, not for pacing my galleries.
starter/remark: I dust the empty plinth every morning. Habit, I suppose.
If that shield ever comes home, I'll bake the biggest cake in Varrock.
Years we've searched for that shield. Years! Not so much as a rivet.

starter/compliment: Oh, it's you! The one who made friends under the castle.
Sigmund hid the silverware, they say. You found him out, I'll bet.
You arrived not knowing the way, and now there's a treaty.
starter/insult: All that peace, and you still march through here like it's a war.
Friend to goblins now, are you? Mind they don't pick up your manners.
I'd thank you properly, but you never stand still long enough.
starter/remark: Below ground's theirs, except the cellars. Those are ours, I think.
Goblins under the castle! I wave down the cellar steps of a morning.
Quieter than adventurers, goblins. Much kinder to the floors.

starter/compliment: A face that wants neither directions nor a casket. How refreshing.
Look at that one. Came through here green as grass, once.
You didn't make me jump at all. Most strangers make me jump.
starter/insult: Adventurers. Always in a rush, and not one of them waves.
Must you stride in like that? I thought it was that man again.
Seen ever so many come through, and you're... well, one of them.
starter/remark: If anyone asks, I'm not resting. I'm inspecting the flagstones.
Still can't hear a raised voice without thinking of that awful man.
Treasure hunters again. Why does every scroll send them to me?

starter/compliment: Thank you for not treading rubble about. I swept all day.
That one'd not run screaming from an earthquake. Not like some.
You've a steady look. I'd want you about if the ground shook again.
starter/insult: Heavy-footed, aren't you? I thought the cellar was going again.
Not you who knocked the cellar wall in, is it? You've the elbows.
That one would be first out the gate if it shook again. After me.
starter/remark: An earthquake, the Duke says. I never felt it, but he'd know.
Funny sort of earthquake, just the one wall. Lucky, really.
Rubble, rubble, rubble... I'm a servant, not a mole.

starter/compliment: On behalf of the Emir, good day to the one who brought his son home.
The Emir is too frail to say it himself, so I shall. Thank you.
Water for you, whenever you wish. It is the least we can offer.
starter/insult: A friend of Al Kharid, yes. The windows are still not a door.
Do not expect a statue. We are a wealthy city, not a foolish one.
Our gratitude is boundless. Our treasury, I must remind you, is not.
starter/remark: Scrabbling at the windows again. Not our rescuer, I do hope.
We have water, and now we have our prince. A rich city indeed.

starter/compliment: A visitor with manners. Al Kharid is always glad of those.
Ah, a traveller who walks round the palace, not up it. Thank you.
Not one complaint about the heat from you. I shall tell the Emir.
starter/insult: Do not even think of the window. We have doors, you know.
Visitors usually bow. Or nod. A nod would do.
With respect, you strike me as a person who climbs things.
starter/remark: Count the wells before the coins, I always say.
Someone has been climbing in at the palace window again. Disgraceful.
The Emir's Arena cost us dearly. I have the accounts to prove it.

starter/compliment: Travelled far, I think, and kept your head. Admirable.
starter/insult: Are you capable? Do not answer, one can usually tell.
I am looking for someone who can get a job done. I shall keep looking.
The palace needs someone capable. Do not take that personally.
starter/remark: How does one tell the Emir that his son is still not found?
Osman has his methods. I have learnt not to ask what they are.
The accounts can wait. The prince cannot.

starter/compliment: Osman does not trust easily. If he trusts you, so do I.
There goes the one who answered for the prince. Every courtesy, now.
Your reward is ready whenever the prince is. I have every confidence.
starter/insult: I would offer you water, but I fear you would stop to drink it.
The prince is still not home. I mention it only in passing.
We are paying a reward for this, you understand. Not a pension.
starter/remark: Someone is finally doing something. I may even sleep tonight.
The prince's rooms are aired and ready. Optimism, or habit.
The reward is counted and waiting. I counted it twice.

starter/compliment: Merlin, look! Our Grail-finder's back!
There goes the finest quester at Camelot. Don't tell Lancelot.
Welcome back, brave knight! The Grail's home, thanks to you.
starter/insult: You did take your time finding the Grail. Still, it's here now!
starter/remark: I've moved the Grail twice today. It looks best by the window.
Must write to Percival. Do kings of the Fisher Realm get letters?
The Grail, here at Camelot! I keep going to look at it.

starter/compliment: Lancelot would find you a terrible bother. High praise, that.
You'd hold your own at the Round Table, I shouldn't wonder.
You'd make fine company at dinner. Better than Lancelot, anyway.
starter/insult: Aha! Another adventurer. We do have a few of those already.
Brave, I'm sure. My knights are braver, but they've had practice.
Do wipe your feet. This was Lord Sinclair's floor before it was mine.
starter/remark: Has anyone seen Bedivere? He was here a moment ago.
Merlin's the clever one. I'm just the one with the crown.
Our own land won't be needing us for a good while yet.

starter/compliment: Aha! Now there's a would-be knight if ever I saw one.
Gawain, look. That one has the makings of a knight.
I can tell a knight in the making. Lancelot can't, but I can.
starter/insult: Fancy a knighthood? So does everyone who passes, it seems.
Lancelot would ask what you've ever done. I shan't, of course.
You're welcome at court, of course. Only knights sit at the table.
starter/remark: Court isn't the same with Merlin glittering away upstairs.
How does a wizard get himself stuck in a crystal? Honestly!
We carried him all the way up from that cave. Heavy, crystal.

starter/compliment: Brave of you to go anywhere near Morgan's keep.
Lancelot doubted you. I'm rather looking forward to his face.
There goes the one who'll free Merlin. I'd stake my crown on it.
starter/insult: Aha, the quester returns! With Merlin? No. Ah well.
Morgan's keep is south, my friend. You did know that?
Still no Merlin? He's not getting any less crystal, you know.
starter/remark: Morgan Le Faye. I should have guessed it'd be Morgan Le Faye.
Sir Mordred, guarding a sorceress's door. Of all things.
The knights all blame Morgan. I'd quite like to blame her too.

starter/compliment: Had I a medal for rescuing priests, citizen, I would consider it.
I have forgiven you the dog, citizen. Very nearly. A royal kindness.
You did well at Paterdomus, adventurer. Apart from the dog.
starter/insult: Next time a priest wants looking in on, I shall send a dog lover.
Only you would rescue a priest by slaying his dog first, citizen.
Run along, citizen. The Salve is seen to, and so, alas, is the dog.
starter/remark: Drezel free, the river blessed, and not a coin spent. Splendid.
Soldiers for Paterdomus, yes, yes. Once other priorities are balanced.
The temple wants soldiers, and the treasury wants a rest. Hmm.

starter/compliment: Aeonisig, that is the shield-finder. Do try to look grateful.
You claimed a reward older than you are, I expect. Well done, citizen.
You found what my father never could. He might have knighted you.
starter/insult: Aeonisig, lock the treasury. The shield-finder is back.
Ah, the one who emptied my treasury. Kindly touch nothing else.
Two of you claimed that reward, I recall. You were the lesser half.
starter/remark: A shield in two halves, held by two gangs. How very like Varrock.
At last I have paid my father's reward. I had not budgeted for it.
That reward outlived my father, and very nearly outlived me.

starter/compliment: Misthalin is fortunate in some of its citizens. Possibly in you.
Serving your king is reward enough, and you look the serving sort.
You may tell people the King nodded at you, citizen. I have, just now.
starter/insult: Aeonisig, have the silver counted once this one has gone.
Another adventurer wanting something from the crown. How novel.
You must be new to palaces, citizen. One does not gawp at the King.
starter/remark: Captain Rovin takes orders from nobody but his king. Quite right too.
Some of my subjects say I am not much of a king. Quietly, I trust.
The queen has views on the curtains. I have learned to share them.

starter/compliment: A capable sort! My father would have had you hunting that shield.
Aeonisig, there is a sensible face. Not in any gang, one trusts.
You might yet earn my father's reward, citizen. Stranger things have.
starter/insult: Aeonisig, does that one look like a shield-finder? Nor to me.
My father waited his whole reign for that shield. I see I shall too.
You would not know the Phoenix Gang if they took your boots, I expect.
starter/remark: Heaven knows what a gang wants with a shield. To hang over the fire?
My library has a whole book on that shield. I have not read it.
Somebody will claim my father's reward one day. Then I must pay it.

starter/compliment: I told the goat about you. It stopped chewing for a whole minute.
Need a cook, my friend? You know where I am, burning things.
Nobody brings a bucket of milk like you do, my friend.
starter/insult: I'd let you cook for the Duke, but he likes his food edible.
Oh, it's you. I'd just got the kitchen tidy.
Use the range by all means, only don't burn anything. That's my job.
starter/remark: Saved! I still say it to myself of a morning.
The range is behaving, or I'm behaving. One of us is.
You can use my range whenever you like now. Not the goat, though.

starter/compliment: I tested you with a birthday that wasn't. You passed, and then some.
My friend, the big cheeses owe you their lives. Not that they'll say.
Ooh, it's you! The Culinaromancer's done for, and so nearly were we.
starter/insult: Mind you don't touch that old cookbook. Look what happened last time.
You never asked if it was really the Duke's birthday. Trusting sort.
starter/remark: Franizzard Van Lumbcook. Big boots to fill, and I've small feet.
It was never the Duke's birthday. I still don't know when it is.
Plain cakes from now on. Burnt, I expect, but plain.

starter/compliment: If you're ever hungry, come by and I'll make you something. Not cake.
The goat would like you. The goat doesn't like anybody.
There goes a helpful sort. Not that I'd ask... well, I might.
starter/insult: Don't come in here after food. It's all burnt, and spoken for.
Off to sea, are you? Rather you than me, with all those eyepatches.
You're not a salesman, are you? Only the last one sold me that range.
starter/remark: Millie's flour is lovely. It's what I do to it that's the trouble.
Temperature control and magic, the salesman said. Smells of smoke.
Wonder what the Duke's table looks like with food that isn't burnt.

starter/compliment: Somewhere about you there's a bucket. I can feel it.
You look the capable sort! The sort who'd know where a cow is.
You'd not let a man be thrown into the street. I can tell.
starter/insult: Don't stand there sniffing. Nothing's cooking, nothing at all.
Oh, don't mind me. I'm only about to lose my job.
The one day I need an adventurer, and I get you.
starter/remark: I can't even go for flour. Who'd mind the kitchen, the goat?
If I stand very still, maybe nobody will ask about the cake.
Thrown into the street, that's me. Hat and all.

starter/compliment: Bold adventurer! I knew it the moment I saw you. Well, I hoped it.
If ever you need garlic, adventurer, mine's yours. All of it.
Oh! It's you again! Have I thanked you today? Thank you!
starter/insult: Don't let it go to your head. I did all the reading.
starter/remark: Still named after him, this village. Somebody ought to see to that.

starter/compliment: Oh! You look ever so bold, bolder than me, which isn't hard.
You don't jump at shadows, do you? I jump at everything.
You've nerve, you have. I've been looking for nerve all my life.
starter/insult: Brave, or just not read the legends? I'd guess the second.
Don't stand so near my door. Things follow adventurers home.
Heading north, are you? Rather you than me.
starter/remark: Did that shutter just move? Wind, probably... probably wind.
Garlic's going soft. I'll need fresh, to be safe.
Many tried to slay him. I've a list of them somewhere.

starter/compliment: I've waited ages for someone who looks like you. Bold, I mean.
Oh, at last, an adventurer with sense! Everyone here is so calm.
You'd not laugh at a man for keeping garlic, would you? No.
starter/insult: Not afraid? Everyone should be, and nobody is.
Plenty tried and failed with the Count. You'd fail quicker, I expect.
Walking about so carefree, with a vampyre just up the road?
starter/remark: Everybody says he's harmless. Well, he'd want them to.
Generations since he left the manor. He's saving himself, mark me.
Not since I moved here, he hasn't. But that's just it, isn't it?

starter/compliment: I'd lend you my garlic, but I can't spare it. Well, a clove.
Saradomin be with you. I'll be upstairs, with the garlic.
That's the one going after the Count. Not a tremble on them.
starter/insult: All that hoping I did, and it's all riding on you... oh dear.
Did you even go to the Blue Moon, or just drink there?
I could've done it myself by now. Well, no... but someone could.
starter/remark: Any day now... any day, and I can open the shutters.
If it goes wrong, I'm moving somewhere with no manors.
Told the neighbours help was coming. They just shrugged.

starter/compliment: Guards, a salute, please. There goes the one who saved our Tree.
If every human were like you, I'd have had no war to call off.
You killed a black demon in my tunnels. I shan't ever forget that.
starter/insult: Glough warned me about humans. Some days I almost see his point.
One black demon, and you've been strutting about ever since.
You did leave the mine as you found it, I hope? Mostly?
starter/remark: Daconia rocks in my own roots, and me none the wiser. Harumph.
Daero learns so quickly. A far better head guardian than the last.
I very nearly went to war with the humans. On Glough's word alone.

starter/compliment: Great Guthix, a polite human! Do stay as long as you like.
Let that one through, please. A guest of the Grand Tree.
Welcome to Ta Quir Priw, traveller. You're as welcome as anyone.
starter/insult: Harumph! Do mind the roots, traveller. They were here first.
Harumph. You humans do clomp so on the ramps.
You'd make a fine gnome, traveller, give or take a few feet.
starter/remark: Is it a crunchies night or a batta night? Decisions, decisions.
My dinner from Aluft Gianne's is late again. A king can wait.
Oaknock built most of this place. I only have to keep it standing.

starter/compliment: A visitor, with the Tree so poorly! You're braver than you know.
Kind of you to call, with half the Stronghold glaring at humans.
Leave that one be. Not every outsider is a saboteur.
starter/insult: Don't lean on the Tree, please. It has quite enough troubles.
Harumph. Whatever ails the Tree, trampling its roots won't help.
If you're the saboteur, you're a poor one. You came in by the front.
starter/remark: Glough's been strange since his wife died, poor fellow.
Glough's the best guardian I have. If even he can't save it...
Half the town's nervous of humans now. That isn't like us.

starter/compliment: All the way to Hazelmere with a bit of bark! You're a good sort.
I'd swear the Tree stands a little straighter when you're about.
There goes our helper. See the guards give them no trouble.
starter/insult: Harumph. Still no word on the bark? The Tree won't wait forever.
Mind where you tread near the foundations. They're older than you.
You did take the translation book? Hazelmere won't say a word else.
starter/remark: Hazelmere helped grow this tree. If he can't read the bark, who can?
Hazelmere only speaks the old tongue. I hope that book's up to it.
Sabotage by humans, Glough says. I'm not convinced. Not yet.

starter/compliment: Best passenger I ever wrecked.
You gave old Ned his last ship. Well, his latest.
You stood that deck like you were born to it. Mind, it was sinking.
starter/insult: Heroes get songs. Captains who got 'em there get seaweed.
Killed a dragon and still buys rope off somebody else, I'll bet.
Wrecked on Crandor, home on a whale, and did you so much as wave?
starter/remark: Lost a ship, found a whale. The sea gives and takes, it does.
Saw a dragon close up, and my hair's still its own colour. Mostly.
That whale... never asked its name. Rude of me, really.

starter/compliment: Anything you want in wool, old Ned's yours. Bar jumpers.
There goes the one who smuggled a prince out in old Ned's wig.
You knew where to come for a wig. Clever, that. Old Ned's the best.
starter/insult: A wig! I sailed the seas, and you had me doing hair.
Folk'll think old Ned's gone soft, making wigs for the likes of you.
You'd make a poor prince, you would. Wig'd slip off at the gate.
starter/remark: If a wool wig can fool a kidnapper, think what my rope could do.
Ned's Handmade Wigs, I could call it. Royal custom, an' all.
Never thought old Ned's wool would sit on royalty. Itchy, I'd expect.

starter/compliment: Brave, I'd say. Not monster-brave like me, but brave enough.
Decent sort, you. You'd not ask old Ned to knit.
You look like someone who knows good rope when they sees it.
starter/insult: Hemp, is it? I've seen how you look at my rope.
Tie a knot? You'd tie a granny, if you gets me.
You'd be green over the side before we'd left harbour.
starter/remark: Dry land doesn't roll, doesn't creak. Unnatural, I calls it.
Salt on the wind? No... that's the pig-sty.
Sea's behind me, they say. Sea's never behind a sailor.

starter/compliment: If you ever needs a captain, old Ned's still got his sea legs.
Nobody'll give old Ned a ship, but they'd give you one, I'd wager.
That one'd make a fine first mate. Better than them as turned me down.
starter/insult: Course that one'd get work at sea. Young and daft, but young.
Too old, they tell me. You look too green, if anyone asks me.
When you're old and nobody'll hire you, you'll understand.
starter/remark: Asked at the docks again. They looked at my knees.
Grey hair's the sea's doing, not the years. Someone tell 'em.
Gulls go out to sea every morning. Nobody tells a gull it's too old.

starter/compliment: I do not trust people. You I distrust a little less.
You walk past the palace as though you belong. You have earned it.
starter/insult: Do not ask me for sq'irk juice. I have barely enough for myself.
starter/remark: I keep a short list for dangerous work. It is shorter than one thinks.
Juice before noon? A spymaster must keep his fingers light.
She gives me no more fruit. We had words, once. That is all.

starter/compliment: I have filed you under 'possibly useful'. Do not make me refile you.
Not a word out of you as you passed. I approve.
You remind me of myself, long ago. Before I had the sense to stay put.
starter/insult: If you are trying to look inconspicuous, do keep trying.
That one would sell the Emir's secrets for a kebab. Watch them.
They say adventurers can keep a secret. They say a great many things.
starter/remark: Every Menaphite knows my face. I take that as a compliment.
Nobody stands outside a palace all day for the view.
The Chancellor would trust a camel if it bowed nicely.

starter/compliment: A stranger who does not gossip. Rarer than rain, in this city.
Not a hero, I think. Something more useful than that.
You did not ask what I do here. Already you are ahead of most.
starter/insult: Subtle as a camel in a tent, that one.
Word is the Chancellor will hire anyone. I see the word has spread.
You? Hassan would hire you. That is precisely the trouble.
starter/remark: Hassan sends me every stranger with a sword. I sift them.
I know more of the prince than I say. That is rather the point.
The Emir's heir taken. Someone was careless, and it was not me.

starter/compliment: Good. You have told nobody. I would know if you had.
There is a spy's patience in you somewhere. Keep it till Draynor.
You heard the whole plan without interrupting once. Remarkable.
starter/insult: Do try not to start a war. It is a key, not a siege.
If Keli spots you first, I shall deny ever having met you.
So you are the hope of Al Kharid. How very... brave of us.
starter/remark: Dressing the prince as Keli is absurd. That is why it will work.
East of Draynor, of all places. Bandits have no taste in jails.
Keli calls herself a lady. I have met camels with better manners.

starter/compliment: A dragon slayer at my door. Sit, if ye must. Briefly.
Best the Guildmaster ever sent me. Don't tell him I said so.
Real deeds, that one. Not like the fancy-pants lot.
starter/insult: Apologised once. Ye'll not get another out of me, adventurer.
One dragon slain, and still ye can't haggle a master smith down.
starter/remark: A visage, now. Dragonkin made, they say. Rarer than a quiet day.
My plate's finally for sale. Only took a dragon.
Shield soaks up the fire, and it goes... where? That's what I'd know.

starter/compliment: Not much swagger on you. I'll grant you that much.
Not one of the Guildmaster's peacocks, are ye?
starter/insult: Don't ask me how to kill anything. That's the Guildmaster's job.
Prices go up for folk who stare. Mine do, anyhow.
Wilderness is just up the road, if ye're bored. Do us both a favour.
starter/remark: A master smith charges what he likes. That's the point of being one.
Folk call me odd. Odd's better than chatty.
Ghost Town, they used to call this place. Quieter then, I'll bet.

starter/compliment: Might be sommat in you after all. Might.
Short and to the point, you. I like a short visit.
Thought you were another fancy-pants. No... you'll do.
starter/insult: Fancy-pants hero, are we? I'll believe it when I see a dragon's head.
Hero, that one? Not slain so much as a chicken, I'd wager.
Rune platemail's for heroes, and I don't see one.
starter/remark: Cliff behind me and fools in front. 'Tis a hard life.
Grand Exchange sells everything, they say. Not my armour, it don't.
Heroes, they call themselves. Not a dragon between 'em.

starter/compliment: Bit less swagger on you since I mentioned that dragon. Good.
Still in one piece? Crandor hasn't had you yet, then.
You went and took it on. Didn't think ye would.
starter/insult: Ask the Guildmaster how to kill it. I'm not yer nursemaid.
Cold feet, is it? Crandor's not getting any closer.
Dragon's on Crandor, not in Edgeville. Ye might've noticed.
starter/remark: A dragon for a platebody. Fair trade, by my reckoning.
If they come back wi' the dragon slain, I'll eat my words.
Wonder if that last one's been eaten yet.

starter/compliment: Aspirant! Your page has grown so, I've had to sew another in.
I've underlined your name. I never underline anything.
Nobody reads my pages. For you I'd nearly make an exception.
Ocellus himself, and the Aspirant still standing. A fine entry.
There goes the one who took the Nexus. Write that down... oh, I did.
starter/insult: Another visit, another line. I'm running out of ink on you.
I wrote 'heroic' by your name. Then I added a question mark.
The records are impressed. I'm reserving judgement.
Your page is long now, Aspirant. Long and, in places, repetitive.
starter/remark: A busy chapter in the records, the Nexus. I've had to add pages.
Guthix's guardians, a page each. Ocellus gets two, and a warning.
I keep the alliance's progress. I don't always keep it in order.
Ocellus, Guardian of Ascension. Now how is that spelt...

starter/compliment: A promising entry, this one. Very promising, I shall underline it.
Aspirant! The records are very keen on you, and so am I, I think.
Such purposeful steps. Those will look splendid on the page.
The alliance struggles, and in walks the Aspirant! I'll write that.
Your page is filling up nicely. No, you may not see it.
starter/insult: A short entry, yours, Aspirant. I've written longer notes to myself.
Ah, the Aspirant! At least, I'm fairly sure it's the Aspirant.
Dawdling, noted. The records are very thorough, Aspirant.
The records expected the Aspirant days ago. Still, here you are.
starter/remark: Every step in this lobby goes in the records. Every... single... one.
Hands off the pages! Ah, you weren't touching them at all.
My apprentice is at those crystals again. He'd better be taking notes.
People call me 'a' record keeper. As if there were others!
The archive's secrets, all in these pages. Somewhere in these pages.

starter/compliment: Arrav himself would tip his hat to you, if the tales are true.
Let's see... shield found, reward paid. And by you! Ah, yes.
You did history a kindness, friend. It so rarely gets one.
starter/insult: A gang member, in my library? I'll be counting the books tonight.
Half a shield! Was the other half too heavy for you, I wonder?
Joined a gang for the sake of history. I'd have simply read about it.
starter/remark: Arrav's shield back in the museum. The histories were right, for once.
Half with each gang, all those years. Wright never guessed that.
The king paid up, I hear. I do hope he read the certificate himself.

starter/compliment: A reader, I'd wager. You've a thoughtful sort of face, stranger.
Careful hands, I see. The sort that bring a book back in one piece.
Interested in history? I could tell from the door, you know.
starter/insult: Adventurers only come in here to ask the way out. Every one of them.
I'd lend you a book, stranger, but I'd like it back, you see.
Reading isn't catching, you know. You could try it quite safely.
starter/remark: I'd read in here even if they didn't pay me. Don't tell the king.
People borrow books and return pressed flowers. Not the books, mind.
The Imcando dwarves loved redberry pie. History's full of pie.

starter/compliment: I'd lend you the shield history, stranger. You've an honest face.
There's a sharp look about you, stranger. Fond of a puzzle, I'd guess.
You've a reader's patience about you. That's rarer than courage.
starter/insult: Another one who thinks a library's for standing out of the rain.
Do you know who Arrav was? Ah. Well, there's a book.
You look like you'd lose a shield faster than the museum did.
starter/remark: A stolen shield and a gang split in two. Better than most romances.
That history of the shield... now which shelf did I give it?
Then the Black Arm lot split from the Phoenix... gangs are like that.

starter/compliment: Ah, the shield-hunter. You'll be a footnote in the histories, surely.
Been to see Baraek, have you? Good. Most people only buy furs.
Brave of you, poking about after gangs for the sake of history.
starter/insult: Asking Baraek about gangs? I'd have bought a fur first, to be polite.
If the histories ever mention you, it'll be in very small print.
You, in a gang? I can't picture it, and I've a fine imagination.
starter/remark: Baraek and the Phoenix Gang, I heard. A fur trader! Who'd think it?
Did I send them to the right fur stall? There's only one, I believe.
The shield history's out on loan. Or behind the goblin tribes.

starter/compliment: Thank you for being there when Juliet... ermmm... you know.
Without you I'd never have met Phillipa, so golly, thank you!
Wooooo! My favourite friend! Second favourite. Phillipa's first.
starter/insult: You were meant to save Juliet, weren't you? Ermmm... never mind.
starter/remark: Ermmm... was it a crypt or a cellar? Somewhere damp and sad, anyway.
I'd be a hero if I weren't frightened of ghosts. Well, one ghost.
Saw Juliet's ghost again! Up on the balcony! I ran ever so fast.

starter/compliment: Have a flower! No, wait, they're for... somebody. Have a sniff, then.
Kind face! I'd tell you my troubles if I could remember them.
Oh, it's you! At least I think it's you. Hello anyway, my friend!
starter/insult: Have we met? You've a very forgettable face. Not that I remember any.
Looks as lost as I am, that one. That's quite lost.
You look the sort who gets court summonses. I get them too!
starter/remark: A message? No, a court summons. They always are.
I went to school with Father Lawrence. Or someone very like him.
The square, then the general store, then... where was I going?

starter/compliment: That one walks like a hero. I walk like a man carrying flowers.
You'd understand love, I can tell. Do you? I can't tell, actually.
You're nearly as lovely as Juliet! Not quite. Close, though.
starter/insult: Oh. You're not Juliet. Never mind, you're still... somebody.
You look like a court summons, my friend. Official and frightening.
You'd never get up a balcony. Neither could I. We're alike!
starter/remark: Flowers for Juliet again. She'll throw them back. She's a good arm.
Her name's Juliet, I'm almost sure. It begins with a J, anyway.
I'll wait in the square. Love waits in squares, I think.

starter/compliment: My dearest, bravest messenger! What was your name again?
You're braver than me. You'd walk right past her father!
You've not got a face like a father. That's the nicest thing I know.
starter/insult: Did you forget the message? I'd forget the message. We're so alike!
Wait, are you her father? You're not? Then why the stern look?
You took your time! Or I did. One of us is late, my friend.
starter/remark: Her father's sworn to kill me. I'd hide, if I knew who from.
Is that him? Is that her father? No... a baker. Probably.
Should I wear a disguise? I'd only forget I was wearing it.

starter/compliment: There goes the one who turned the tide. Let them pass, quietly.
You gave this city something real to hope for. Not a myth.
You killed Ranis Drakan, my friend. The ghetto will tell it for years.
starter/insult: Every vampyre in Meiyerditch must know your face by now. Well done.
I've a power I can't control. You've a temper you won't. Some pair.
Reckless again. I'm too tired to keep counting you back in.
starter/remark: Mekritus, Andiess, Flaygian. I say their names before I sleep.
My own blood, used against my own people. I cannot wash that off.
Three empty bunks below. I've not had the heart to clear them.

starter/compliment: A hidden laboratory, and you just walked in. Of course you did.
Without you, those sketches would still be half a castle.
You are welcome at our table, such as it is. Mind the rats.
starter/insult: Find another secret laboratory if you like. Just don't drink anything.
Next time you meet Vanstrom, perhaps bring a friend. Several.
You walk through Meiyerditch like it's market day. It isn't.
starter/remark: Myreque prevail. It sounds less like a prayer these days.
We have their castle on paper. Now we need a plan worth the ink.
Why would Sarius save anyone? Nothing in this city is a gift.

starter/compliment: My friend, you'd have made a fine runner in the ghettos.
Sven could sell you a disguise, but I think you'd bluff instead.
You have the look of someone people would follow. Careful with that.
starter/insult: I admire recklessness. From a safe distance, mostly.
Old Man Ral would call you a fool. Kindly, but he would.
You'd be spotted in a ghetto before you'd taken a step.
starter/remark: Myreque prevail. I have said it so often it has worn smooth.
Trader Sven's disguises have served us before. Itchy things, though.
We told the world what happens in those ghettos. The world nodded.

starter/compliment: Every time you come back alive, the whole base breathes again.
My friend, you'd pass for a local if you looked more frightened.
With you here, that castle looks a little smaller.
starter/insult: If you're caught, I have never met you. Myreque prevail.
Sven's disguises fool the vyrewatch. Your walk might not.
You can't just stroll past the vyrewatch, my friend. Well. You did.
starter/remark: Castle Drakan never sleeps. Neither, lately, do I.
Pull the silver lever and down we go. Home, such as it is.
Ral finds us papyrus. Nerve we have to find for ourselves.

starter/compliment: A mother sleeps at night because of you, friend. No small thing.
A rescuer who still pays the toll. You are a credit, friend.
I sell waterskins to many. I tip my hat to very few, friend.
starter/insult: Saving girls in the desert is good work. So is paying for a robe.
The cell is still there, friend. Heroes have been known to need it.
starter/remark: Ana is home, and already eyeing the dunes again. That girl!
Next time Ana passes, she reads the billboard first. Twice.

starter/compliment: Ah, effendi! I would wager you actually read the billboard.
I would trust you with the bank chest, effendi, and I trust nobody.
Something tells me the sands will give you back, effendi.
starter/insult: Did I not lock you up once? No? My mistake, effendi.
So long, effendi. I shall keep a cell warm for you.
You will come back thirsty, effendi, and you will blame me.
starter/remark: My guards say my price is very reasonable. I do pay their wages.
The cell is empty today. I always find that suspicious.
The gate needs mending again. Sand gets into everything, even hinges.

starter/compliment: There goes someone a mother could trust. Not many come through here.
starter/insult: I would sell you a pass, effendi, but I would rather sell you a robe.
Irena needs a hero. Let us both hope one comes along soon.
Mind you do not get lost as well, effendi. One is enough.
starter/remark: Days, now. The desert does not give people back after days.
No word of Irena's girl. Outlaws would not dare... would they?
That girl went south, and my gate has not seen her since.

starter/compliment: If anyone can bring that girl home, effendi, I would bet on you.
Irena talks of nobody but you now, friend.
You gave a mother hope. That is worth more than any pass I sell.
starter/insult: Do not come back without her. Well, do come back, but with her.
Irena's hopes rest on you. I would walk a little faster.
So long, effendi. Try not to be the next one Irena waits for.

starter/compliment: Ah, our agent! Err... our friend. Simply a friend, naturally.
Asgarnia owes you a debt, friend. The order can scarcely pay it.
You broke only what needed breaking, friend. I am most grateful.
starter/insult: A spy who fights with cabbages. Heaven knows what the charter says.
Honour obliges me to thank you again. Honour can be very tiresome.
No knighthood for a cabbage, friend. Things are not that dire.
starter/remark: Let them sulk in their fortress. They have earned a good sulk.
That fee for the fortress business has left the order lighter still.
Years their witch spent on that potion. Years! Spoilt by a vegetable.

starter/insult: Err... you are not one of my squires, are you? No, they salute.
Honour forbids me to say what I think of your timing, friend.
Sir Burrus has taken against this one. He is usually a fine judge.
starter/remark: Err... where did I leave the charter? Sir Burrus looks guilty.
Every Black Knight knows my knights by sight. So much for stealth.
Regent of Asgarnia, and still nobody brings the ale.

starter/compliment: I would wager no Black Knight has ever heard of you, friend.
Saradomin sends help in odd shapes. Yours will do nicely.
starter/insult: Falador under threat, and its visitors come to look at the furniture.
I have five years of errands for anyone who stands about like that.
My corgi has more fight in him, I suspect, and he is asleep.
starter/remark: My ale has gone warm while I read their demands. Again.
Someone ought to slip into that fortress. Someone nobody knows.
The charter forbids spying. The charter did not foresee this.

starter/compliment: Asgarnia is in your hands just now, friend, and they look steady.
I knew a stranger would serve better than a knight. I was right.
It is good to see you, friend. Mind who is listening.
starter/insult: A fine time to admire the view, friend, with the realm under threat.
Err... you are meant to be in the fortress. Are you in the fortress?
Spies are meant to be unseen, friend. I can see you quite clearly.
starter/remark: If the spy is caught, the order knows nothing of it. Err... naturally.
The longer the silence, the bigger that weapon grows in my head.
Their weapon is bluster, I expect. Saradomin, let it be bluster.

starter/compliment: I'd say how proud the order is of you, old bean, but it's a secret.
One of ours now, that one, though nobody's to know it.
Should you ever die, old bean, you'll wake in Falador. Much nicer.
starter/insult: Do try not to die in Lumbridge, old bean. Frightful swamp.
That one sat the tests empty-handed and came out a little cleverer.
You squeaked into the Temple Knights, old bean. By a whisker.
starter/remark: Must have a word with Sir Amik about briefings. Again.
Sir Vey Lance will be pleased with the latest one. Brains, at last.
Spiffing weather for a new knight, what? Not that anyone's to know.

starter/compliment: There goes a brainbox, if I'm any judge, and I usually am.
Top-hole! Somebody in this town who isn't dumb muscle.
starter/insult: Bit of dumb muscle, are we? Never mind, the world needs those too.
Jolly good show, walking past. Most people manage it too, mind.
Muscles are all very well, but one does like a brain to go with them.
starter/remark: Another day on the bench. Somebody has to keep an eye on things.
Haw haw haw! Oh, the things one hears from a park bench.
I'd sooner sleep in a hedge than spend a night in Lumbridge.

starter/compliment: Now there's somebody who reads more than the notice board.
Oh, top-hole. A stranger with their wits about them, at last.
Spot of brains on that one, haw haw. Must remember the face.
starter/insult: Bit of a plodder, what? Still, plodders get there in the end.
One can see the cogs turning, old sport. Slowly, but turning.
starter/remark: Lumbridge folk keep wandering in here. The swamp follows them.
Sir Amik sends his squire for ale before breakfast, I hear. Haw haw!
That corgi of Sir Amik's is a Sir, dontchaknow. Haw haw!

starter/compliment: Jolly good show finding me, old bean. Half Sir Amik's lot get lost.
Sir Amik put your name forward, and for once he chose well.
Too clever by half for the White Knights, that one. Haw haw!
starter/insult: Good heavens, still here? Most recruits have passed or fled by now.
Still dithering, old bean? The tests won't sit themselves.
That one's thinking. One can hear it from the bench, haw haw.
starter/remark: Any fool with a sword can be a White Knight. We want the other sort.
Mind your head on the way down, I always say. Nobody listens.
Secret order, and here I sit on a park bench. Best hiding place going.

starter/compliment: Good day to you, traveller! Even strangers look cheerful to me lately.
My sword is home and the visitors are polite. A good day all round.
starter/insult: A sword like mine needs a hand like mine. Yours would drop it.
Not every stranger gets to stand near an Imcando blade. Do stand back.
starter/remark: Asrol brought it back without a mark on it. Good lad.
My family sword is back where it belongs. Five generations, unbroken.
Same sword my father held. I would know it anywhere.

starter/compliment: A White Knight in my armoury, and a keen one. As it should be.
Every Black Knight you fell is a rank closer to Master, knight.
Should you reach Adept, knight, I shall be very glad to serve you.
